relation.rationale: Difference in the representation of the umlaut (bͤ vs boͤ).
The difference is the presence of the letter 'i' in 'neigung' versus its absence in 'negung', representing a spelling variation of the same word.
Difference in the prefix spelling (eyn- vs eynge-), same grammatical form and meaning.

Difference in the spelling of the verb 'sollen' (2nd person singular imperative/subjunctive): 'solt' vs 'solst'. This is a variation in the final consonant cluster (t vs st) representing the same grammatical form, typical of early modern spelling variation.
The difference is the presence of an extra 'r' in 'Oberkerkeitlichs' vs 'Oberkeitlichs', which is a spelling variation of the same word.
The difference is the presence of a superscript 'r' (abbreviating 'gebür' or similar) in one reading versus its absence in the other, which is a graphic/orthographic variation.
The readings are a hyphenated fragment and a page number, which do not correspond as variant readings of the same text unit.
Difference in the spelling of the verb prefix (e- vs er-), same grammatical form.
Difference in the representation of the umlaut (wͤg vs waͤg).
Different words with different meanings (more vs. should/were)
The words 'undern' and 'andern' are distinct lexical items with different meanings (under/underneath vs. other), not merely variant spellings of the same word.
Difference in the representation of the umlaut (diaeresis) over the vowel o.
Difference in long s (ſ) vs short s (s) and u/v (u / v) in the same word.
The prepositions 'in' and 'zu' are different words with different meanings.

Different verbs (legen vs. leben) with different meanings
The words 'kaͤuſcher' and 'künſcher' are distinct adjectives with different meanings (likely 'coarse/rough' vs 'artificial/cunning'), not just spelling variants of the same word.
The prepositions 'in' and 'zu' are different words with different meanings.

The difference is a hyphenation break (Be- vs Beſchließlicher) where the word is split across lines in one edition but not the other, or simply a difference in line-breaking/hyphenation representation.
